web_evidence.note: The author’s official Chapter 1 transcript has Carl identify himself and continuously narrate his actions and history as “I.”

web_evidence.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl official Penguin sample
web_evidence.note: The authorized 46-page sample spans Chapter 1 and substantial narrative after Carl enters the dungeon; scene narration remains consistently in Carl’s first person around embedded System messages.

web_evidence.title: Book review of Dungeon Crawler Carl by Matt Dinniman

Searched “Dungeon Crawler Carl first person narrator” and “Dungeon Crawler Carl point of view”; opened an explicit whole-book review describing the first-person perspective.

Checked publisher catalog material, fan references, forum results, and a Grimdark Magazine interview result; catalog synopsis grammar was not treated as person evidence, fan/forum assertions were unnecessary, and the interview page failed to open.
person_note: Carl is the participating controlling narrator and tells the story as “I.” The diagnostic quote containing “I said” agrees with two sustained authorized excerpts and an explicit whole-book review. Most sampled second-person language comes from the dungeon System’s achievement, item, and creature-description interface, while other first-person forms occur in dialogue; these are embedded local voices rather than alternative base narration. No credible evidence of sustained narration in another person was found.
